claims.text: THE CREDENTIAL LIST AS A COURT DOCUMENT. Lazar's Pre-Sentence Report of 27 July 1990 records his reported education as '1978, Bachelor of Science Degree in Physics and Electronic Technology, Pacifica University'; '1982, Masters of Science in Physics, MIT'; '1985, Masters of Science in Electronic Technology, Cal Tech'. The document is Tier 1 for what it shows, which is what he reported about himself to a court, and it is the reason the credential question is evidence rather than rumour.

claims.text: The conviction and its dates. Arrested for pandering in Las Vegas on 5 June 1990; pleaded guilty to felony pandering on 18 June 1990; sentenced on 20 August 1990 by District Judge Jack Lehman to probation, 150 hours of community service, an order to 'stay away from brothels and undergo psychotherapy', with one year of psychotherapy specified, the judge saying he 'could not make a determination regarding his claims'.

claims.text: The 19 June 1990 report records the police account of the offence: that Lazar recruited a prostitute, operated her business from the Newport Cove apartments, maintained computer records of customers and their licence plate numbers, and took at least half her earnings. It records the sentencing exposure as 'one to six years, with a possible fine of $5,000'. It also records, from police records, that 'Lazar told her he had master's degrees from two universities', which is the same credential claim appearing in a police file rather than a broadcast.

claims.source: Douglas Dean Johnson, 'Bob Lazar and his Nevada felony: Some key documents', 31 January 2021, https://douglasjohnson.ghost.io/bob-lazar-and-his-nevada-felony-conviction/ , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: The 1996 proceedings. Douglas Dean Johnson, who obtained the file, establishes that Lazar received a three-year suspended sentence with probation which he completed; that in 1996 he petitioned to withdraw the guilty plea citing post-traumatic stress, hidden federal records and inadequate legal representation; that the District Attorney urged the court to deny the petition, arguing 'that Lazar's new claims were irrelevant to his admitted and documented criminal activity'; and that the judge denied it. Lazar remains a convicted felon.

claims.source: Gene Huff, reply posted 15 May 1995, https://www.dreamlandresort.com/area51/lazar/hf-acad.htm , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: The rebuttal, carried and not adopted. Gene Huff, replying on 15 May 1995 to Tom Mahood's post quoting the report, says the Pacifica entry is the probation officer's misinterpretation: that Lazar claimed only to have 'took an English course and a history course' from Pacifica University by correspondence, and that he 'had to petition for his diplomas because he had hodgepodged all of his classes from various institutions'.

conflicts: The disposition is described differently by two reliable routes. The Las Vegas Review-Journal of 21 August 1990 reports probation with 150 hours of community service and psychotherapy. Douglas Dean Johnson, working from the court file, describes a three-year suspended sentence with probation, completed. These are compatible readings of a single disposition but they are not the same wording, and no session has reconciled them against the judgment of conviction itself.

desc: THE COURT RECORD IS THE SPINE OF THE LAZAR QUESTION AND IT SHOWS TWO SEPARATE THINGS, THE SECOND MORE USEFUL THAN THE FIRST. The first is a conviction: Lazar was arrested on 5 June 1990, pleaded guilty to felony pandering on 18 June 1990, and was sentenced on 20 August 1990 by District Judge Jack Lehman to probation with 150 hours of community service, an order to stay away from brothels and a year of psychotherapy, the judge remarking that he 'could not make a determination regarding his claims'. In 1996 Lazar petitioned to withdraw the plea, the District Attorney opposed on the ground that his new claims were irrelevant to admitted and documented criminal activity, and the court refused, so the conviction stands. The second thing the file shows is what makes the credential question Tier 1 rather than gossip. Lazar's Pre-Sentence Report of 27 July 1990 records his own reported education: a 1978 Bachelor of Science in Physics and Electronic Technology from Pacifica University, a 1982 Master of Science in Physics from MIT, and a 1985 Master of Science in Electronic Technology from Caltech. That is not a television claim that can be blamed on a paraphrasing journalist. It is what he told a court under sentence, in writing, through a probation officer. Every institutional check since has failed to confirm any of the three. Gene Huff's rebuttal of 15 May 1995, that the probation officer misunderstood a pair of correspondence courses, is carried beside it and is not adopted.

timeline.label: Lazar arrested for pandering in Las Vegas
timeline.text: Mahood's timeline records the arrest on 5 June 1990. The offence, per the police account printed in the Review-Journal a fortnight later, was recruiting a prostitute, operating her business from an apartment complex, maintaining computer records of customers and their licence plate numbers, and taking at least half her earnings.

timeline.label: Guilty plea to felony pandering
timeline.text: Lazar pleaded guilty to felony pandering in District Court. The Las Vegas Review-Journal reported it the next day under the headline 'Source in Channel 8's UFO series pleads guilty to pandering charge', by Warren Bates, page 8B, noting the exposure as 'one to six years, with a possible fine of $5,000'.

timeline.label: Pre-Sentence Report records the Pacifica, MIT and Caltech credential list
timeline.text: THE SPINE OF THE CREDENTIAL QUESTION. Lazar's Pre-Sentence Report of 27 July 1990 lists his own reported education: '1978, Bachelor of Science Degree in Physics and Electronic Technology, Pacifica University'; '1982, Masters of Science in Physics, MIT'; '1985, Masters of Science in Electronic Technology, Cal Tech'. Because this is a court document rather than a television statement, the credential question is Tier 1 evidence and not gossip. No institution has confirmed any of the three. Gene Huff's rebuttal of 15 May 1995, that the probation officer misread two Pacifica correspondence courses, is carried beside it and is not adopted.

timeline.label: Sentenced by Judge Jack Lehman to probation, community service and psychotherapy
timeline.text: District Judge Jack Lehman sentenced Lazar to probation rather than prison, with 150 hours of community service, an order to 'stay away from brothels and undergo psychotherapy', and a year of psychotherapy, saying he 'could not make a determination regarding his claims'. The same report describes Lazar's claim as of that date as being that 'the U.S. government was testing alien spacecraft at the Nevada Test Site, 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas', which is a different named place from the one the claim later settled on.

timeline.label: Petition to withdraw the 1990 guilty plea is refused
timeline.text: Lazar petitioned to withdraw the plea, citing post-traumatic stress, hidden federal records and inadequate legal representation. The District Attorney opposed, arguing 'that Lazar's new claims were irrelevant to his admitted and documented criminal activity'. The judge denied the petition and the conviction stands.

The Pre-Sentence Report as an image or a certified copy. It is quoted at one remove, by Tom Mahood in 1995, and Gene Huff disputed the interpretation rather than the existence of the passage the next day, which is the strongest corroboration available from what was opened.

The name of the woman named in the 1990 police record is deliberately not carried on this board. She is a private individual with no relation to the programme and no node, claim or edge here names her.
